//: Per-version upgrade records applied by `update` to already-installed harnesses. Keys are released versions; each entry may carry: removed (stale template paths to delete when sha-unmodified), renamed (old path -> new path), promotedModules (opt-in modules folded into the default harness), configSteps (gate steps injected into the consumer's gate config: {name, cmd, after, array}; array defaults to VALIDATE_STEPS — the floor chain — and is 'STOP_HOOK_STEPS' for the non-floor turn-fatal checks. harness.config.mjs is SEEDED, so `update` never overwrites it: this injection is the ONLY way a new step reaches an existing install), configCommandUpdates (from-guarded canonical-command rewrites: {name, from, to}), seedOnInitOnly (NEW seeded exemplar paths a newer template ships as init-time-only starting content — `update` must NOT auto-plant them into an existing install; a trailing '/' matches the whole subtree, no slash matches an exact file; collected across ALL versions, not just pending, and pullable on demand via `update --refresh-seeded <path>`). seedOnInitOnly is a PURE list of path patterns read by a matcher — never put a comment string in it; a stray entry ending in '/' would silently withhold an entire subtree (scripts/check-seeded-migrations.mjs asserts every pattern names a path the template actually ships). Entries are applied in version order for manifest.harnessVersion < v <= installer version. See installer/lib/migrations.mjs.

THE MULTI-TENANCY RELEASE. The governing rule for this record is one sentence: an `update` must leave an existing install GREEN. Five gates are injected, and every one carries an adoption seam keyed on the manifest's baseVersion — so what this record has to get right is which FILES arrive.

Two failure modes, in opposite directions. Plant a migration and `update` has put unapplied DDL in front of a live database, which check-migrations.mjs's append-only git-diff check then reads as history appearing out of order, and which the next `supabase db push` would apply to production. Withhold a file a gate FAILS CLOSED on and the injected step reds on the first validate after the upgrade. So every path below was classified by one question, answered by READING the gate: what does it do when this file is absent?

PLANTED (three files, deliberately absent from seedOnInitOnly). tools/tenancy.json and tools/db-limits.json are hard failures when missing — the contract and the ceilings must exist as reviewable data before any schema is judged against them, and that check runs before any ramp. tools/security-headers.json is planted so that an install which later pulls apps/web/lib/security-headers.ts with --refresh-seeded gets a gate that judges it, instead of one that fails closed on a missing policy. None of the three names a project-specific table, column or procedure; all three are contracts, ceilings and posture.

WITHHELD — DDL. supabase/migrations/*, supabase/schemas/*, supabase/seeds/ and the audit pgTAP suite. The tenancy-adoption runbook (expand->contract, dual-scoped policies alongside the owner-scoped ones, an expiring `until`) is the sanctioned path in. The db-scale CI lane reads baseVersion for exactly this reason: pre-0.2.0 skips loudly, 0.2.0+ FAILS if the seed is missing, so withholding cannot become a way to switch the plan probe off.

WITHHELD — reviewed data whose ROWS name this project's own tables, columns, procedures and functions. security-definer-allow.json, audit-columns.json and pii-columns.json all read absent-as-empty, which is the safe default in each case (no definer registered; metadata-only audit capture). A deny-list of columns another schema does not have denies nothing, and thirteen paragraphs about functions another database never created is thirteen paragraphs of foreign prose in someone else's PR. rate-limit-budget.json is withheld for a STRONGER reason: check-rate-limits.mjs ramps on its ABSENCE, so planting it would both hand the install a budget naming procedures it does not have AND switch off the ramp that was protecting it. db-perf-baseline.json carries per-TABLE cardinality floors, and the template's names `notes`.

WITHHELD — generated artifacts and the code that generates them. tools/generated/query-shapes.json and packages/verticals/notes/src/data/query-probes.ts travel together or not at all: the manifest is a recording of what THIS DAL executed, so planting it beside a different DAL yields a regen-diff that can never converge, because regenerating from zero probes cannot reproduce it. gen-query-shapes.mjs treats 'no probes and no manifest' as nothing to record — which is exactly the tree this pair leaves behind. packages/platform/supabase/src/database.types.ts is the same shape of mistake with a wider blast radius: it is generated from the running database by `pnpm db:types`, and planting a types file describing orgs, memberships, audit and quota makes tsc describe a schema the consumer's database does not have.

WITHHELD — the 0.2.0 web surface and the rate-limit package. Exemplar app code in the ordinary sense: a consumer's apps/web has its own routes, and an unreferenced page reds route-manifest and dead-code on their next validate. apps/web/lib/security-headers.ts and apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts are here deliberately — both gates ramp on the module's absence, so withholding them is what keeps the gate quiet until the consumer adopts the seam. packages/platform/ratelimit/ is a new workspace package plus an Upstash dependency, and the ADR's whole point is that this is a deliberate choice, not a default.
0.2.0.removedWhy: Not a deletion — a REPLACEMENT, using the one mechanism that can reach a stale seeded file. This test ships with the gate-a11y-deep module and was authored by the harness, and the version 0.1.3 shipped imports `MockRouteHandler` from apps/mobile/src/testing/mock-server.ts, which does not export it and never did. It is `seeded` (it lives under apps/), so `update` skips it forever and the consumer keeps a test that cannot compile. `removed` deletes it BEFORE the plan loop runs, and the loop then plants the corrected template copy because the path is absent and not seedOnInitOnly. The deletion is sha-guarded: a consumer who edited the file keeps it and gets a note naming the conflict, which is the right outcome — a hand-tuned a11y test is theirs, and silently overwriting it would be the failure this whole ownership model exists to prevent.

//: THE METAL-PRESET RELEASE. Two changes reach the template; neither reaches an existing install by default, and that is the record.

The design-token preset seam: DESIGN_TOKENS rides the placeholder rails (prompted at init, carried in manifest.answers; `update` backfills 'default' into pre-0.2.1 manifests, which ARE default installs by definition). The metal variant lives under template/presets/tokens-metal/ — OUTSIDE base/stack/modules — so a default install's `update` never walks it: the preset is init-time-only BY CONSTRUCTION, not by registration, and deliberately contributes nothing to seedOnInitOnly (check-seeded-migrations grounds patterns against base/stack/modules, where preset paths do not ship).

The design-system-native generator contract, completed: gen-preset.mjs, the committed tailwind-preset.cjs, and the freshness test are the three files src/preset.ts always documented and 0.2.0 never shipped. seedOnInitOnly, not planted: all three install under the seeded packages/ prefix, and the committed preset is rendered from @app/design-tokens — planting template bytes into an install whose (seeded) token source may have been retuned would red the new freshness test on their next validate. Pullable via `update --refresh-seeded packages/design-system-native/`.

THE CLOSED-SURFACE RELEASE. The governing finding is one sentence: the harness's enforcement surface was not closed over itself, and in several places it CLAIMED enforcement it did not perform. Every gap this release fills was green on 0.2.1 — not because a rule judged it safe, but because no rule looked. What that means for an `update` is unusual and is the whole reason this note is long: most releases add checks over the CONSUMER's code, and this one adds checks over the INSTALL ITSELF, so the honest question for every file below is not 'will this red their code' but 'does this install still have a thing to check'.

TWO INJECTED STEPS, and both are placed before anything expensive. `wiring` (step 3) asserts the enforcement layers are CONNECTED — six hooks wired, the permission posture, `pnpm validate` still running the gate, CLAUDE.md a pure include, VALIDATE_STEPS containing its frozen floor, and CODEOWNERS covering every escape list and enforcement-surface prefix. Those five invariants had exactly one check between them (`installer doctor`) and NOTHING RAN IT. `secrets` (step 4) is a hermetic credential scan: lefthook prints `SKIP secrets scan` without the gitleaks binary and gitleaks.yml only scans after a PUSH, so a turn could end green with a service-role key in a tracked file on any machine without the tool.

PLANTED, and each because its gate FAILS CLOSED without it. tools/approved-tools.json is the MCP registry the new pretool-mcp-guard reads; an absent registry is not an empty policy, it is no policy, and the guard denies every mcp__ call while pointing at a file that is not there. It ships SEEDED (installer/lib/layout.mjs) for the reason the 0.2.0 record gives for the reviewed-data files: the guard's own deny message asks the consumer to add a row, and an `owned` file under tools/ is sha-pinned, so the harness would be demanding an edit and then calling that edit tampering. Its integrity is the write-guard rule plus gate-integrity's escape-list dirty check. tools/secret-patterns.json and tools/doctrine-symbols.json are harness-AUTHORED detection data (a credential-shape list, a closed retired-token map) and stay `owned` so improvements keep reaching installs. tools/stop.floor.json is the frozen Stop chain and must be `owned` — it is the floor.

TOLERATED-ABSENT, deliberately, and this is the 0.2.0 plant-vs-withhold hazard repeated on purpose. tools/retrofit-accept.json and tools/secret-scan-allow.json are REVIEWED ACCEPTANCES: each converts a red into a NOTE for one specific finding. Both gates read them absent-as-empty, so shipping an empty one would ship a reviewed-acceptance file nobody reviewed, and an install with no retrofit conflict and no secret finding has nothing to accept. Neither appears below because neither ships at all; both are write-guard-protected and in gate-integrity's ESCAPE_LISTS, so CREATING one is a reviewable commit.

THE ONE THING AN UPGRADE CAN GET WRONG HERE, stated plainly. .claude/settings.json is `owned`, and 0.3.0 rewrites it: every hook command becomes `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/..."` (the executable bit leaves the trust path), the write-guard matcher gains NotebookEdit, and a sixth hook (pretool-mcp-guard, matcher `mcp__.*`) is added. An install that TUNED its settings has drift, so `update` keeps theirs and parks ours under .harness/pending/ — correct, and it means the MCP guard is not wired on that install until a human merges. `wiring` reports exactly that, and it is RAMPED to 0.3.0, so the finding arrives as a dated NOTE rather than a red on the update that delivered it. `doctor` names the parked file until it is reconciled.

EVERY NEW CHECK IS RAMPED except two, and the exceptions are the point. The eslint rules `local/no-unverified-session` and `local/service-role-edge-functions-only` ship LIVE: a pre-existing violation of either is an authentication bypass or an RLS bypass, not a style debt, and a release that discovered one and then withheld it for two versions would be choosing the wrong thing to protect. Everything else — the gate-integrity config surface, the commit-not-dirty rule over the threshold configs, `wiring`'s findings, the approved-tools doc lockstep, the doctrine token map, the enforcement-tiers shape check — carries a deadline (`until`), because 0.3.0 also makes ramps EXPIRE: `rampNote` now requires one, measured against harnessVersion rather than baseVersion, so an escape can no longer be held open by simply never graduating. Pre-existing 0.1.x/0.2.0 ramps expire in 0.4.0; everything introduced here expires in 0.5.0. THIS RELEASE SHIPS THE CLOCK, NOT THE ALARM — nothing reds on a deadline in 0.3.0.

THE ALARM RELEASE. 0.3.0 shipped the clock and dated every pre-existing escape 0.4.0; this is the release where those deadlines arrive. It adds NO configSteps: nothing joins VALIDATE_STEPS or STOP_HOOK_STEPS. What changes is that twelve call sites already IN the chain stop withholding their findings on installs whose baseVersion predates them. An `update` to this version can therefore leave an install RED, and that is the designed outcome rather than an accident.

WHO IT REDS, exactly: every expiring ramp opens at minVersion 0.2.0 and rampNote is inert once baseVersion >= minVersion, so the affected population is baseVersion BELOW 0.2.0 — among released vintages, only 0.1.3. A 0.2.0, 0.2.1 or 0.3.0 install meets no deadline here; those checks have been live on it all along. Do not take the count from these notes: `pnpm validate 2>&1 | grep "RAMP EXPIRED"` is the only honest answer for a given tree, and nine of the twelve are ADOPTION seams that fire only when the surface is genuinely absent. The remediation is one path, printed by every layer: sweep, `graduate`, re-run. docs/runbooks/harness-upgrade.md now carries a section per expiring gate.

WITHHELD — apps/web/__tests__/*.test.ts, the six seed suites that make the new `web-unit` vitest project non-vacuous. They name THIS project’s own lib modules, and a consumer’s apps/web is theirs. diff-coverage’s new apps/web/lib surface is RAMPED at minVersion 0.4.0 precisely so withholding them cannot red anyone: the gate notes the absence and expires in 0.5.0, by which time `update --refresh-seeded apps/web/__tests__/` is a documented pull.

WITHHELD — apps/web/lib/action-outcome.ts, and the reason is the one the upgrade lane exists to find. It is a NEW seeded module extracted from a clone, so plant-when-absent would deliver it to an existing install; but its only callers are the seeded Server Actions under apps/web/app/actions/, which `update` must never rewrite. The result on a real 0.2.1 install was a planted file nobody imports and a RED `dead-code` step — the harness handing a consumer an orphan and then failing them for it. Withheld, an upgraded install keeps its existing inline folds and stays green; a fresh install gets the extraction and the duplication gate that now reaches apps/web keeps it honest.

NOT WITHHELD, and it needed a code change instead — eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y. eslint.config.mjs is harness-OWNED so `update` refreshes it, but package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml are SEEDED and mergeWorkspaceYaml runs only under `init`: a new plugin dependency has NO channel to an existing install. A static import in the refreshed config resolved to nothing and killed the entire `lint` step — not one rule lost, the whole gate. The config now resolves the plugin dynamically and omits the block when it is absent, and tools/check-wiring.mjs says so out loud: hard at baseVersion >= 0.4.0, a dated NOTE below it naming `pnpm add -Dw eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`. Selftest Canary 29 proves the rules still fire on a fresh scaffold, so "resolves" cannot quietly become "resolves and does nothing".

TOLERATED-ABSENT — tools/migrations-allow.json, new here and deliberately not planted. It acknowledges a finding on APPLIED history that cannot be swept: the ADR reference and the lock_timeout preamble both live inside the migration, and the append-only rule reds any edit to a committed one, so the expiry would otherwise be a red whose only in-file remedy is a different red. The gate refuses an entry for a migration that is new at the diff base, so it covers history rather than authorship. Creating it is a widening: it is in ESCAPE_LISTS and must be committed.
vitest.config.ts, eslint.config.mjs, knip.json and every tools/check-*.mjs are harness-OWNED and refresh with no record needed.

rampExpiry.//: Recorded RETROACTIVELY in 0.5.0, when scripts/check-ramp-ledger.mjs gained the assertion that a release's stated population must equal its computed one. The prose above said 'only 0.1.3' from the day 0.4.0 shipped and it was correct — but nothing compared the sentence to the call sites, so it was a claim rather than a control. This is the same sentence as data.
rampExpiry.why: Every escape expiring in 0.4.0 opens at minVersion 0.2.0, and rampNote is inert once baseVersion >= minVersion, so only installs whose baseVersion predates 0.2.0 meet a deadline. Sweep the RAMP EXPIRED findings (`pnpm validate 2>&1 | grep 'RAMP EXPIRED'` is the only honest count for a given tree), then `graduate`. docs/runbooks/harness-upgrade.md carries a section per expiring gate.

0.5.0.//: 0.5.0 the accounting release. dependencyObligations is a NEW record kind and this is its first use. THE HOLE, in the 0.4.0 record's own words above: eslint.config.mjs is harness-OWNED so `update` refreshes it, but package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml are SEEDED and the workspace-catalog merge runs only under `init` — so a new plugin dependency had NO channel to an existing install, and the static import of eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y resolved to nothing on every upgraded tree, killing the whole `lint` step. 0.4.0 patched the symptom (dynamic resolution + a dated NOTE at check-wiring.mjs:305) and left the cause; that NOTE expires in THIS release, so the remedy has to exist. `update` does NOT write these files — both are SEEDED, and a tree whose pnpm-lock.yaml no longer matches its manifests fails the `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` the shipped workflows run twelve times. It parks a machine-readable obligation at .harness/pending/dependencies.json, names it in the report, and `doctor` reds until the consumer applies it and reinstalls.

dependencyObligations.name: eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y
dependencyObligations.why: eslint.config.mjs resolves it dynamically and applies every rule at error over apps/web. Without the pin the plugin is absent, the a11y half of the `lint` step silently enforces nothing on the web surface, and check-wiring.mjs reds once its 0.4.0 ramp expires in this release.

rampExpiry.//: THE SECOND ALARM, and a wider one than 0.4.0's. 0.4.0's expiring escapes all opened at minVersion 0.2.0, so only baseVersion 0.1.3 met a deadline. The eight expiring here open at 0.3.0 (four in docs-sync, one each in gate-integrity and wiring) and at 0.4.0 (diff-coverage, and the wiring a11y seam), so the population reaches every vintage BELOW 0.4.0. A 0.4.0 install meets nothing: it is the only released vintage this release does not red, which is also why scripts/ci/upgrade-lane.sh keeps its default leg — leg A is the only one that reaches `graduate`'s success branch, and replacing it with older baselines would introduce a break and delete its proof in one act.
rampExpiry.why: Eight escapes close. Four are docs lockstep (AGENTS.md's gate list after an injected step, the approved-tools registry/doc pair, the doctrine token map, and the enforcement-tiers shape); the other four are gate-integrity's hash coverage of the enforcement CONFIGS, check-wiring's whole CODEOWNERS finding set, check-wiring's web a11y plugin seam, and check-diff-coverage's per-file floors over apps/web/lib plus the layered packages. The a11y one is the only expiry whose remedy the harness itself has to deliver: this release's dependencyObligations record is that remedy, and `doctor` reds until it is met. Sweep, then `graduate`. docs/runbooks/harness-upgrade.md carries a section per expiring gate.
